A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same work, with directly matchable methods and experiments. V1 includes supplementary Sections 7–10, Table 4 and Figures 11–14; these are absent from the supplied v2, which ends after the references despite retaining references to supplementary material.

before.justification: V1 reports original MULAN benchmark results, an 18-participant foreground-preference study, ablations, qualitative comparisons and supplementary diagnostic results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark and user-study results and adds comparator scores, numerical foreground metrics and further ablations.

M1.justification: The FLUX.1-Fill-dev backbone, foreground/background mask contexts, multimodal latent fusion, LoRA adaptation and RGBA decoding remain unchanged. The added ablations evaluate existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: Training still uses MULAN foregrounds, LayerDiffuse-generated foregrounds and OpenImages backgrounds. Evaluation retains MULAN object removal and real-world foreground extraction/layer decomposition; the additional metrics and ablations do not establish new dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the evaluated background-removal comparators from SD-XL Inpainting, PowerPaint and FLUX.1-Fill-dev to also include BrushNet, OmniEraser, GeoRemover and Qwen-Image-Edit. The foreground comparators remain MattingAnything and DiffMatte.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and FID evaluation of foreground extraction, previously assessed through user preferences. Table 3 introduces controls omitting synthetic foregrounds or individual modalities. Existing training settings and stated evaluation sample sizes remain unchanged; the new foreground metrics' computation and reference data are insufficiently specified.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of the synthetic-foreground training contribution and separate edge, segmentation and depth contributions, extending the existing backbone, context and LoRA ablations. Conversely, v1's supplementary VAE-reconstruction validation and illustrated failure cases are absent from the supplied v2, substantially changing the available diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2 adds result entries without changing the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds four comparator rows, twelve foreground metric values and four ablation rows. Newly reported foreground metrics favor DiffMatte over Ours, including PSNR 29.69 versus 28.38 and FID 28.50 versus 39.52, whereas unchanged preferences favor Ours, 59.51% versus 32.34%. Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged; additional supplementary comparison and diagnostic outputs are absent from v2.

T1.justification: The task formulations, token-concatenation definitions and O(KN) attention-complexity argument are retained. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear in the supplied v2.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting inpainting models, efficient training, multimodal context and state-of-the-art performance. The revised contribution bullet restates data and parameter efficiency already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: The explanations of context-guided preservation, multimodal guidance and the LoRA tradeoff remain substantively unchanged, as do Section 5's failure conditions. The new synthetic-data ablation supports the existing hybrid-data rationale; v2 offers no substantive interpretation of the foreground metric ranking versus user preferences.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page URL, although the PDF alone does not establish code or data availability. V1's prompt categories, examples and approximately 300 prompts per category are absent from v2. The main implementation details and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for the four new comparators and several diffusion/video-model works. Section 2.3 emphasizes accessibility through LoRA and multimodal conditioning, while retaining the central positioning against LAYERDECOMP's full fine-tuning approach.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized related-work and experimental rewrites, shorter captions, an affiliation/internship note and omission of the supplementary sections. V2 also introduces an unresolved FLUX citation in Section 4.1.

P2.justification: Table 2 is redesigned from a preference-only comparison into a method-by-metric table; Tables 1 and 3 expand, Table 3 moves, and LPIPS direction markers are corrected. The supplementary prompt table and four figures disappear from the supplied document, substantially reducing its visual evidence, while main Figures 1–10 are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons and targeted ablations strengthen validation, and the new foreground metrics reveal a useful contrast with user preferences. However, their evaluation protocol is underspecified and the differing rankings are unexplained, while v1's supplementary prompt details, foreground comparisons, VAE validation and failure illustrations are missing from v2. These material gains and losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
